Implementation: - Core rule: src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts implements the annotation format validation logic and is explicitly traced to this story: - File-level and function-level JSDoc include: - @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md - @req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION, REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION, REQ-PATH-FORMAT, REQ-REQ-FORMAT, REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT, REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING, REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY - The exported rule has standard ESLint shape { meta, create } with: - meta.type = "problem" - meta.docs.description = "Validate format and syntax of @story, @req, and @implements annotations" - meta.messages: invalidStoryFormat, invalidReqFormat, invalidImplementsFormat, invalidRuleConfiguration - meta.schema = getRuleSchema() from helpers
Core requirements: - REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION: - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts defines canonical regex patterns: - getDefaultStoryPattern(): /^docs\/stories\/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV/[\w-]+\.story\.md$/ - getDefaultReqPattern(): /^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$/ - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts uses these via resolveOptions() and options.storyPattern/options.reqPattern to validate collapsed annotation values for @story, @req, and @implements. - JSDoc on create() includes: "@req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION - Implement formatting checks per specification".
- REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION: - finalizePendingAnnotation() decides whether pending.type is "story" or "req" and dispatches to validateStoryAnnotation() / validateReqAnnotation(): - JSDoc: "@req REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION - Validate annotation syntax matches specification". - validateStoryAnnotation(): - Trims rawValue; if empty → reports invalidStoryFormat with buildStoryErrorMessage("missing", ...). - Collapses whitespace via collapseAnnotationValue() and validates against options.storyPattern. - Handles multi-line values and auto-fix path suffix when safe. - validateReqAnnotation(): - Similar pattern for @req, using options.reqPattern and buildReqErrorMessage().
- REQ-PATH-FORMAT (story path rules): - Default storyPattern requires a relative path under docs/stories with .story.md extension (see getDefaultStoryPattern()). - validateStoryAnnotation() enforces this regex and uses getFixedStoryPath() for safe auto-fixes: - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts: - getFixedStoryPath() returns null if original.includes("..") (rejects traversal like ../). - Handles missing .md and .story.md suffixes and upgrades plain .md to .story.md. - Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts explicitly cover: - "[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] valid story annotation format (single-line)" with a fully valid path. - "[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] missing story path (single line)" for `// @story`. - "[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] invalid story file extension" and "missing extension in story path" with expected auto-fix output. - "[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] story path must not use path traversal" for `../docs/stories/...` (error, no fix).
- REQ-REQ-FORMAT (requirement ID rules): - getDefaultReqPattern(): /^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$/ in valid-annotation-options.ts. - validateReqAnnotation(): - Missing trimmed value → invalidReqFormat with buildReqErrorMessage("missing", null, options). - Invalid value → invalidReqFormat with buildReqErrorMessage("invalid", collapsed, options). - Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts: - "[REQ-REQ-FORMAT] valid req annotation format (single-line)". - "[REQ-REQ-FORMAT] missing req id (single line)" and "missing req identifier with trailing space". - "[REQ-REQ-FORMAT] invalid req id format (single line)" (value "invalid-format").
- REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT: - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-internal.ts: - PendingAnnotation tracks type, value, hasValue for multi-line annotations. - normalizeCommentLine() trims, strips leading '*' for JSDoc, and slices from the annotation tag if present; this allows multi-line values. - processComment() in src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - Splits comment.value into lines, normalizes each, and passes to processCommentLine(). - processCommentLine(): - On @story/@req line: starts a new PendingAnnotation, finalizing any previous one. - On subsequent lines without new tags but with text, it appends to pending.value and preserves hasValue. - collapseAnnotationValue() in valid-annotation-utils.ts collapses all whitespace, so multi-line values behave as a single string for regex checks. - Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts: - Valid multi-line @story and @req examples (e.g. path split across two lines). - Invalid multi-line examples verifying that after collapse, bad values are reported correctly.
- REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING: - normalizeCommentLine() supports: - Line comments, block comments, and JSDoc (/** ... */) with leading '*'. - Annotation tags appearing anywhere in the line, not only at the start. - processComment() and processCommentLine() rely on normalized lines to manage pending annotations across different comment styles. - Test "[REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING] valid JSDoc-style comment with leading stars and spacing" confirms parsing is robust with extra spaces and leading '*'.
- REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY: - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts: - buildStoryErrorMessage(kind, value, options) and buildReqErrorMessage(kind, value, options) produce detailed, distinct messages for "missing" vs "invalid", embedding the offending value and example text. - Rule meta.messages wrap these details: "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}." for each type. - Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts assert exact message strings, including embedded values and examples, for numerous invalid cases (missing story/req, invalid path/ID, custom examples, config errors).
Integration with other rules and plugin: - src/index.ts includes "valid-annotation-format" in RULE_NAMES and exports it via the rules object, so ESLint can use it with the other traceability rules (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, etc.). - The rule’s create() function operates at Program level and inspects all comments from sourceCode.getAllComments(); this naturally validates annotations discovered by existing function/branch rules, satisfying the integration criterion.
Quality standards and error handling: - Rule structure follows ESLint best practices: meta.type, meta.docs, meta.messages, meta.schema from helper getRuleSchema(). - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts: - resolveOptions() normalizes nested and flat options and compiles regex patterns, capturing invalid patterns via buildInvalidRegexError(). - getOptionErrors() collects these config errors. - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - Program visitor reads optionErrors and reports them using messageId "invalidRuleConfiguration", but still uses default patterns to continue annotation validation. - This demonstrates robust error handling and resilience to malformed configuration.

traceability.notes: The story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md is fully implemented. The valid-annotation-format ESLint rule and its helpers enforce precise yet flexible syntax and format rules for @story and @req annotations (and @implements), including default and configurable regex patterns, multi-line support, robust parsing across comment styles, and detailed error messages for missing and invalid values. The rule is integrated with the plugin and other annotation rules, has comprehensive, story-linked tests that cover all listed requirements, and is documented in depth in docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md with examples that align with the story. Test runs via npm test complete without reported failures. All acceptance criteria and explicit requirements in this story are satisfied.
